audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no real cooldown numbers, and the page never states Colossal Smash's auto-reset tell or that Justice Punch's terrain cuts Lux's retreat since she has no dash.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags both: the P auto-reset wind-up is the dodge cue, and E's terrain blocks Lux's escape path.
audit.corrected: Added real E/W cooldowns to breakdown.cooldowns, and folded the P auto-reset tell and E terrain-retreat interaction into breakdown.early and breakdown.late.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, passive-auto, bank the Q visibly — the chip is free and the threat governs.
edits.after: His W taunt charge is an 18s cooldown at rank 1 — if the first charge whiffs or gets snared, he has no second engage for a long stretch.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown until the hook learns the rhythm — the binding is the lane's law; spend it like one.
edits.after: Flash into W taunt skips the slow charge tell entirely — respect his flash range near your carry or you eat a full engage with no warning.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Read it before every duo step-up. - Your W Prismatic Barrier answers exactly one disaster per cooldown. - Spend the R on swing moments only.
edits.after: - Justice Punch (E): 11s at rank 1, down to 7s maxed — no engage while it's down, read it before every duo step-up. - Shield of Durand (W) taunt: 18s early, 14s maxed — a whiffed charge stays unfunded a while. - Spend the R on swing moments only.

edits.before: Zone with the threat — the button you hold governs more than the one you press.
edits.after: Colossal Smash (P) resets his next auto for bonus damage — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast itself.

edits.before: You decide the fights your team attends — start them, peel them, or poke them out of existence.
edits.after: You have no dash — track Justice Punch near walls, since Galio can cut your retreat through terrain if it's still up.
